skill.name: near-ai-cloud
skill.description: Integrate NEAR AI Cloud private inference, compare privacy modes, and understand NVIDIA NRAS, Intel TDX, and chat-signature verification workflows.
skill.summary: Guide NEAR AI Cloud integration and verify private inference trust claims.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fixed examples, environment-variable credential handling, and attestation terminology. The confirmed items are disclosed outbound requests to NEAR AI Cloud and NVIDIA NRAS, which can transmit prompts, credentials, or attestation material. The verification guide also omits explicit NRAS JWT signature validation, creating a high-confidence attestation bypass risk.

remediation.issue: NRAS JWT authenticity is not explicitly verified.
remediation.suggestion: Require JWT signature verification with trusted NVIDIA issuer keys before accepting any claim, then validate issuer, audience, nonce, timestamps, and per-GPU results.

remediation.issue: Examples send prompts, credentials, and attestation material to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear data-transfer notice and require user approval before executing NEAR AI Cloud or NVIDIA NRAS requests.

remediation.issue: Quick-start clients show inline API-key placeholders.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment-variable examples consistently and warn users not to place real keys in source files, prompts, logs, or version control.

content.user_title: Integrate Verifiable NEAR AI Cloud Inference
content.value_statement: Teams need private inference without losing API compatibility or verifiability. This skill explains integration, attestation checks, model privacy choices, and response signature trust.
actual_capabilities: Configure Python and JavaScript OpenAI clients for the NEAR endpoint.
Compare private and anonymised model options.
Generate nonces and request model attestation reports.
Explain GPU verification with NVIDIA NRAS.
Explain CPU quote and signing-address binding checks.
Outline the chat signature verification chain.
limitations: The skill documents workflows but does not provide a complete verifier implementation.
API access requires a NEAR AI Cloud account and credential.
Model availability, pricing, and identifiers can change.
Privacy assurance depends on complete attestation and signature validation.

use_cases.title: Add private inference
use_cases.description: Configure an OpenAI-compatible application to use a private NEAR AI Cloud model.

use_cases.title: Audit model attestation
use_cases.description: Build a checklist for NVIDIA GPU, Intel TDX, nonce, and signing-address verification.

use_cases.title: Choose a privacy mode
use_cases.description: Compare private and anonymised models for sensitive workloads, cost, context size, and capabilities.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to configure an OpenAI client for NEAR AI Cloud using [language], [model], and an environment variable for the API key.

prompt_templates.title: Compare models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [model A] and [model B] for [workload], including privacy type, context size, cost, and verification requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan attestation checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist for [model] covering nonce generation, NRAS claims, JWT signature validation, TDX quote validation, and signing-address binding.

prompt_templates.title: Review a private architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my NEAR AI Cloud architecture for [sensitive workload] and identify trust assumptions, missing attestation checks, credential exposure, and replay risks.

output_examples.input: Configure a Python client for a private model.
output_examples.output: A setup plan using the NEAR base URL, an environment-based API key, the selected model identifier, and a minimal completion request.

output_examples.input: Explain how to verify a model attestation.
output: Generate a fresh nonce and request the model attestation.
Verify NRAS JWT signatures, claims, nonce, and per-GPU results.
Validate the Intel TDX quote and signing-address binding.

output_examples.input: Choose between private and anonymised models.
output_examples.output: A comparison focused on data sensitivity, provider exposure, cost, context size, capability, and required trust verification.

best_practices: Store API keys in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Generate a fresh nonce for every attestation request.
Verify signatures and hardware bindings before trusting privacy claims.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, source files, or logs.
Do not trust decoded JWT claims without verifying their signatures.
Do not accept GPU attestation without validating the Intel TDX binding.

faq.question: Is the API compatible with OpenAI clients?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure a supported OpenAI client with the NEAR AI Cloud base URL and your credential.

faq.question: What is a private model?
faq.answer: A private model runs inside documented TEE infrastructure intended to isolate prompts and outputs from infrastructure operators.

faq.question: What is an anonymised model?
faq.answer: An anonymised model removes identifying routing information but may not provide the same TEE isolation as a private model.

faq.question: Why is a nonce required?
faq.answer: A fresh nonce binds an attestation to your request and helps prevent reuse of a stale valid report.

faq.question: Does this skill fully verify attestations?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and checklists, but production use requires a complete verifier with trusted cryptographic validation.

faq.question: Can I verify chat response signatures?
faq.answer: The skill explains the trust chain, but detailed request hashing and signature verification implementation is listed as planned work.
